question.text: Per Section 3.1.2 of Chapter 3, a For Profit Enterprise (FPE) CANNOT seek registration or listing with a Social Stock Exchange UNLESS it satisfies what core requirement?

answer.text: It is registered as a Company under Companies Act 2013 (or erstwhile Companies Act 1956) AND complies with SEBI Regulations for issuance/listing of equity or debt securities
It is registered as an LLP under the LLP Act 2008
It has corpus of at least Rs. 10 crore
It obtains CSR certification under Section 135

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 3.1.2 states: 'a For Profit Enterprise (FPE) shall not seek registration or listing with Social Stock Exchange, unless it is registered as a Company under the provisions of Companies Act, 2013 or erstwhile provisions of Companies Act, 1956 as the case may be AND complies with the requirements in terms of SEBI Regulations for issuance and listing of equity or debt securities.' Two conjunctive conditions: Company-form AND SEBI-issuance-compliance. The Trap: Option A (LLP) is wrong — LLPs are NOT eligible FPE form. Option C (corpus) confuses FPE requirement with NPO funding threshold. Option D (Section 135 CSR) is for CSR obligor-companies, not SE eligibility. Cross-Exam Context: XII (SMF) Ch on Issuers covers Company-form requirement. III-A (Compliance) tests ICDR for main-board issuers. XIX-A (AIF) explicitly allows LLP vehicles for funds — don't swap with SSE FPE rules. Assessor's Pro-Tip: For an FPE pre-listing SIA review, obtain CIN (Corporate Identification Number) and cross-verify on MCA21. For Section 8 Companies, also verify the Section-8 licence is alive. LLPs and partnerships applying for SSE must be rejected at scoping stage itself.
